editor.saved: Saved. The displays pick up the layout by themselves.
editor.unsaved: There are unsaved changes. The draft stays in this browser until it is saved or discarded.
editor.stale: This layout has been changed from elsewhere in the meantime.
editor.keepMine: Save my version – overwrite the other
editor.needsAdmin: Editing needs access of level “admin”. Open the address once with “#token=” and the token of that access at the end.
editor.hint: Tap a tile to select it. Drag to move it, use the handles at corners and edges to resize. Arrow keys move, with Shift they resize.
editor.occupied: No room there: tiles must not overlap.
editor.noRoom: There is no free room for “{name}”. Shrink, move or remove a tile first.
editor.unknownType: The editor does not know this kind of tile; its place can still be changed.
editor.badJson: This is not a valid JSON object: {error}
editor.rescaleHint: With conversion the tiles keep their share of the screen. Without it they stay where they are – this adds free room at the edge.
editor.screenHint: Size of the screen the layout is meant for, in pixels – or just the ratio, such as 16 and 9. This view follows it; the display itself always fills its screen.
editor.gridRange: Columns and rows are whole numbers from 1 to {max}.
editor.screenRange: Width and height of the screen are numbers greater than zero.
editor.gridCollides: In the grid {columns} × {rows} tiles would overlap or lie outside. Enlarge, move or remove tiles first.
editor.gridRounded: Not all tiles fit the new grid exactly – their edges were moved to the nearest line. Please check; ↶ takes it back.
editor.nameHint: Lower-case letters, digits and hyphens – the name is part of the display's address (?layout=name).
editor.saveFirst: Save or discard first – then the layout can be renamed.
editor.lastLayout: The last layout cannot be deleted.
editor.renameWarn: Displays that carry “?layout={name}” in their address will no longer find the layout.

chart.area: Fill the area under the line

presence.label: Name

weather.codeHint: Code or icon id from OpenWeatherMap; more precise than the text.

video.streamHint: Id of the stream as set up in the video source.

voice.wakeWordHint: Such as “computer”: the display then listens all the time and carries out what is said after the word.

events.name: Name

events.secondsHint: Without it 10 seconds, with a camera 90.
events.videoHint: Id of a video stream that fills the display behind the panel.
events.signal: Signal only: the displays show nothing
events.signalHint: For programs listening on the realtime channel – such as the monitor control.
events.whenHint: The message appears as soon as the datapoint newly meets the condition.
events.valueHint: For “exactly” also true, false or a text such as done.
events.speakHint: The voice comes from the browser of the display – it has nothing to do with voice control. Sound and voice only work after the display has been tapped once.

picker.more: The first {shown} of {count} – search to narrow down.

sources.choose: Choose a source to set it up – or add a new one below.
sources.undescribed: This plugin does not describe its settings; they can be changed as JSON.

sources.badJson: This is not a valid JSON object: {error}
sources.removeSure: Really remove “{name}”? Tiles that depend on it will show nothing afterwards.

sources.unsaved: There are unsaved changes to this source.

sources.notYet: This source has not been created yet. Enter settings and credentials, then “Create and start”.
sources.noNotes: The source has reported nothing since it started.

system.title: Settings
system.needsAdmin: The settings need access of level “admin”. Open the address once with “#token=” and the token of that access at the end.
system.siteHint: Language and colour theme apply to all displays; open displays pick up a change at once. On a single display the address additions ?theme=… and ?night=… take precedence.
system.siteSaved: Saved – the displays have picked it up.
system.eventsHint: “Someone is at the door”, “The washing machine is done”: what a message does on the displays. It is raised from outside via the API or by itself through a datapoint.
system.eventsSaved: Saved – the messages apply at once.
system.raised: “{name}” raised – the message appears here and on every open display. A display gives sound and voice only after it has been tapped once: before that the browser allows no sound.
system.accessOpen: The API is unprotected: anyone on the network can read, switch and set up. The first access entry protects it.
system.accessHint: Every access entry has a token. A display or a program may do with it what the level allows. The tokens are kept in secrets.json; the core does not hand them out again.
system.name: Name of the access entry
system.removeSure: Remove “{name}”? Displays with this token are locked out afterwards.
system.firstAdmin: The first access entry must have the level “set up”. This page remembers its token so that it is not locked out itself; all other displays have to be unlocked afterwards.

system.freshOnce: The token is shown only now. If it is lost, remove the access entry and create it again.

system.accessHelpText:
An access entry is a secret token with a level: whoever presents the token may read, operate or set up. The token is not bound to a device – the browser of a display remembers it after the unlock address has been opened there once, and sends it along with every request afterwards. Whoever knows the token has the access, from any device.
The name is only a label so that you can tell the entries apart: such as “kitchen” for the kitchen screen, “hall” for the tablet in the hallway, “openhab” for rules of the home automation, “office” for your PC. It appears in the log and in error messages (“The token “hall” may only read”). One entry per device or program makes sense: if a tablet is lost you remove only its entry, all others stay.
The levels: “read” for a display nobody should switch from; “read and operate” for ordinary displays and for programs that raise messages; “set up” additionally for these pages – layouts, sources, settings.
Without access entries the API is open: on the home network everybody may do everything. The first entry closes it – and must therefore be allowed to “set up”, otherwise nobody could change anything afterwards, not even you. For the same reason at least one entry with “set up” always remains. Further entries may have any level.
